status: Draft FHGM base matrix: every sealed manifest vector re-observed against the released FHGFF3 1.2 (v0.6.0) base bytes. FHGM has no released contract, no schemaVersion, no schema URL and no schemas/versions.json entry, and selection rule V7 keeps it that way; this file publishes, adopts and claims nothing. Every outcome recorded below is an observation of development/model/validate_fhgm.py run over a twin derived from the committed vector bytes, re-verified by run_conformance.py --matrix.
decision: maintainer decision 2026-11-15: FHGM supports both released FHGFF3 bases; the sealed 1.1 lane in manifest.json keeps its bytes, expectations and evidence trail unchanged and this lane adds the 1.2 observation alongside it.
base: provenance.json matrixBaseSchema records the v0.6.0 bytes; base-schemas.json registers them for the checker.
method: A twin replaces exactly two header lines of its sealed vector - a v0.5.0 #~schema citation moves to https://w3id.org/fair-bioheaders/fhgff3/v0.6.0 (any other citation, such as the v0.6.0 FHR-Specification alias or raw main, is kept) and #~schemaVersion to 1.2, both in the source's quoting style - and the #~checksum line follows: recomputed when the sealed record says verify, preserved when it says stale so the twin remains a stale-checksum case. Records, pointers and every feature byte are unchanged. A vector declaring FHGFF3 1.0 is evaluated as committed (method as-committed-1-0): its stated identity is the defect and there is no 1.2 form of the claim being tested. The checker is handed both registered base files and the same committed predecessors as the sealed lane, and selects the release each loaded file cites by its schema URL: a 1.2 twin is judged by the v0.6.0 bytes and its 1.1 predecessor by the v0.5.0 bytes it cites, which makes the lane a mixed-identity chain test. The base layer is the v0.6.0 release alone.
